name: The Ancient World
description: The first farmers and cities, Sumer and Babylon, Ancient Egypt, Greece and Rome: the civilisations that invented writing, law, democracy and empire.

checkpoints.name: The first farmers and towns
checkpoints.note: After the ice age, people in the Fertile Crescent start to farm. Villages grow into the first towns, such as Jericho and Çatalhöyük, and copper is worked for the first time.

checkpoints.name: Writing, cities and kings
checkpoints.note: Sumer builds the first cities and invents writing on clay. Egypt is united under one pharaoh, and cities rise along the Indus. The wheel, bronze and the first written laws appear.

checkpoints.name: The pyramid age
checkpoints.note: Egypt builds the pyramids of Giza. Sargon of Akkad founds the first empire, Hammurabi writes his laws in Babylon, and the Minoans of Crete build palaces.

checkpoints.name: The late Bronze Age
checkpoints.note: The New Kingdom pharaohs, from Hatshepsut to Ramesses II, rule an empire. The Hittites and Mycenaean Greece rise, and then the whole Bronze Age world collapses.

checkpoints.name: Iron Age empires
checkpoints.note: Assyria and then Babylon rule the Near East, until Cyrus builds the Persian Empire. Greek city-states spread around the sea, Homer is written down and Rome is founded.

checkpoints.name: Classical Greece
checkpoints.note: Greece beats Persia at Marathon and Salamis. Athens builds the Parthenon and tries democracy, Socrates, Plato and Aristotle teach, and Alexander conquers an empire as far as India.

checkpoints.name: Hellenistic kings and the Roman Republic
checkpoints.note: Alexander's generals share out his empire, and the Ptolemies rule Egypt until Cleopatra. Rome conquers the Mediterranean in the Punic Wars, and Julius Caesar ends the Republic.

checkpoints.name: The Roman Empire
checkpoints.note: Augustus becomes the first emperor and Rome rules from Britain to Egypt in peace for two centuries. Christianity spreads, the empire divides, and the West falls in 476.
